content.title: No cable? No problem. Here’s how to stream March Madness games for FREE
content.text: If you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation. By Joey Chandler | NJ.com March Madness has finally arrived! If you are a cord-cutter looking for ways to stream all the action , we’ve got you covered. Sign up for a DirecTV plan with a free trial to get the best streaming option for all-in-one access to every channel needed to watch the men’s NCAA tournament. DirecTV FREE 5-Day trial Sign up for a free trial to DirecTV to stream all things March Madness. Sign up now Men’s March Madness games will air across four networks: CBS, TBS, TNT and truTV . Your March Madness Streaming Guide Want everything in one place? Sign up for a FREE trial to DirecTV Choice (then pay $59.99 for the first month and $94.99 every month following). Looking for budget-friendly options? You can watch truTV, TBS and TNT games for 24 hours with a Sling Day Pass + Entertainment Extra for $5.99 (truTV is not available with a regular Sling Orange Day Pass). Sling also offers three-day, seven-day and monthly passes. Sling Orange passes include TBS and TNT, but you’ll need the Entertainment Extra add-on to get truTV. You can get the Sling 3-Day Pass + Entertainment Extra for $11.99 and the Sling Week Pass + Entertainment Extra for $17.99. You can find all of the Sling subscription options from Day Pass to 3-Month Prepay here . For Sling’s 3-Day Pass (also called Weekend Pass) and 7-Day Pass (also called Week Pass): You will need to manually add the Sling Entertainment Extra at checkout. It will appear as a pop up toward the top of your browser, select “add Sports Extra,” then click edit and scroll through the add-on options until you see the Entertainment Extra add-on and select that option (as Sports Extra is a different add on). TruTV is not in the Sling Sports Extra, but in the Entertainment Extra, which is why you’d opt for that add-on extra for you day, 3-Day Pass or Week Pass. Want to save with streaming deals? For CBS games: Sign up for Paramount+ Premium for just $2.99 per month for your first two months, then $13.99 every month following. (March Madness games are not available with the Paramount+ Essential plan) For TBS/TNT/truTV and Final Four games: Sign up for a Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max bundle , starting at $19.99 per month. For the NCAA women’s tournament: Sign up for the Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited bundle for $35.99 per month. (Games will air across ESPN networks and ABC)
